hypothesis: Side-aligned visible-book pressure may identify after-cost opportunities withheld only by the completed 5-minute BREAKOUT requirement, but it must first survive prospective, venue-matched, portfolio-compatible observation in both directions.
decision: Retain the authorized v14 runtime and exact 5-minute breakout gate unchanged. The first fresh HYPE candidate was portfolio-deployable and lost 37.0667 bps after taker fees and official funding, directly contradicting the favorable same-run discovery sample. The concurrent SOL candidate gained only 0.1830 bps after costs and is mechanism-only evidence because the real SOL slot was already occupied. Continue both challengers as report-only observers; grant no execution authority and make no sizing, entry, exit, order, or runtime change from this revision.
falsifier: The current retain-the-gate recommendation would be updated if a larger prospective sample contains both long and short deployable HYPE observations, remains positive after full costs with profit factor above one, is not dominated by one path, and preserves realistic top-level capacity. The aligned-book relaxation hypothesis is weakened further by additional deployable net-negative observations, profit factor at or below one, cost-sensitive outcomes, or persistent one-sided sampling. SOL observations become portfolio evidence only when the symbol is flat at the candidate decision time.
limitations: Only one prospective HYPE and one prospective SOL path have resolved, so neither repeatability nor direction symmetry is established.
The only portfolio-deployable observation is the losing HYPE short; its profit factor and concentration metrics are mechanically determined by one sample.
The SOL short is not deployable portfolio evidence because a real SOL position already occupied the one-position-per-symbol slot at decision time.
Both observations are shorts; the bidirectional contract has not yet produced a resolved long after the cutoff.
The observer uses recorded BBO replay, top-level capacity, full taker fees, and official funding, but private IOC latency and adverse selection remain estimated.
The fixed 60-minute horizon and 80-bps adverse-BBO stop proxy evaluate entry selection, not the deployed 8-to-24-hour exit controller.
The HYPE outcome weakens the aligned-book relaxation hypothesis but one loss does not prove the existing 5-minute gate has positive edge.
The live audit prefix contains one open, venue-protected SOL lifecycle and zero current-run closes; its marked economics are provisional.
One evidence file cited by historical revision 1 remains reported as changed; revision 9 does not conceal or reinterpret that integrity drift.
No strategy, position, order, sizing policy, execution scope, venue stop, backend process, or current portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
